title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (v2)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document is Redwood Inference's consolidated guidance for hiring, onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended as the canonical reference for people-ops partners and managers to ensure consistent, fair, and timely candidate and employee experiences.

Scope: Applies to full-time and part-time hires, contractor conversions, interns, and managers across the company.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro: Our process balances candidate experience, quality-of-hire, and speed. Recruiters and hiring managers should measure time-to-offer, slate diversity, and scorecard fidelity.

High-level steps (owners in parentheses):
1. Requisition & approval (hiring_manager)
   - Create req in Workday using approved job template; attach role brief and scorecard.
   - People-ops validates compensation band and headcount within 3 business days.
2. Sourcing & screen (recruiting)
   - Recruiter presents a slate of at least 3 diverse candidates within 10 business days when possible.
   - Recruiter conducts an initial screen to confirm interest, eligibility, and compensation expectations.
3. Interview loop & scorecards (hiring_manager)
   - Follow the standardized loop for the role (technical roles: screen, technical interview, system design, manager interview; non-technical: functional assessment, case study, manager interview).
   - Interviewers submit scorecards in the ATS within 48 hours with numeric ratings and written rationale.
4. Debrief & calibration (hiring_manager + panel)
   - Panel debrief within 3 business days; use rubric to weigh competencies, role fit, and risks.
5. Offer & negotiation (recruiting + people-ops)
   - Target time-to-offer: 14 calendar days from first interview. People-ops drafts the offer letter and shares within 48 hours of approval.
   - Track offer acceptance reasons in the ATS; target acceptance rate: 75%+.
6. Close & onboarding kickoff (recruiting + people-ops)
   - On acceptance, recruiter triggers preboarding checklists and notifies IT, security, and the hiring manager.

Scorecard requirements (mandatory):
- Ratings: Core competencies (role-specific 1-5), Communication & collaboration (1-5), Problem solving (1-5), Ownership & impact (1-5), Cultural fit (1-5).
- Overall recommendation: Hire / No hire / Consider.
- Written strengths, risks, and examples discussed.

Diversity & inclusion expectations:
- Recruiters aim to present diverse slates; hiring managers should request alternate slates if diversity goals are not met.
- For senior roles, include at least one interviewer outside the hiring manager's direct reporting chain.

Hiring SLAs & metrics:
- Time-to-fill (target 30 days)
- Time-to-offer (target 14 days)
- Offer acceptance rate (target 75%+)
- Interview-to-offer ratio (goal <= 5 interviews per offer)

2) Employee onboarding (preboarding through 90 days)

Intro: Structured onboarding improves ramp, retention, and early impact. People-ops owns the program; managers own role-specific ramp plans and weekly check-ins.

Preboarding (before start) - owners: people-ops, IT
- Send welcome packet and first-week agenda at least 5 business days before start.
- Provision core accounts (Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Workday, code repos) and confirm access 48 hours before start.
- Ship hardware and confirm delivery with tracking information.

Day 1 & first week - owner: manager
- Manager welcome: clarify role expectations, initial 30/60/90 goals, and first tasks.
- Team welcome and buddy assignment (buddy for first 90 days).
- Orientation with people-ops covering benefits, payroll, and security training.
- Systems access verification checklist completed.

30/60/90 plan (manager deliverable within 3 business days of start):
- 30 days: complete onboarding tasks and deliver a small, demonstrable outcome.
- 60 days: make independent contributions on a project with peer feedback.
- 90 days: take ownership of a component/feature and have a formal 90-day review with manager.

Ongoing check-ins & surveys:
- Weekly 1:1s for the first 12 weeks (manager responsibility).
- 30-day pulse survey (people-ops) and 90-day manager review to confirm fit and development plan.

Documentation & templates (people-ops library): New Hire Checklist, 30/60/90 Plan, Remote Onboarding Checklist.

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Principles: Continuous feedback, transparent evidence-based assessments, and calibrated ratings. Managers are responsible for coaching and collecting evidence for evaluations.

Cadence & components:
- Quarterly informal check-ins and goal updates.
- Annual performance review: employee self-assessment, manager assessment, and calibration panel.
- Promotion cycle: semi-annual; dates published by people-ops.

Typical annual review timeline:
1. Self-assessment window opens (2 weeks).
2. Manager draft assessments due (2 weeks).
3. Calibration panels convene (1 week).
4. Final ratings published and sign-off by people-ops.
5. Manager one-on-one to discuss outcomes within 2 business days of finalization.

Rating guidance and guardrails:
- Standard scale: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement.
- Managers must support ratings with evidence: measurable results, examples, and competency notes.
- For any rating below Meets Expectations, managers must provide a written development plan and involve people-ops.

Continuous feedback expectations (manager responsibilities):
- Provide timely, actionable feedback during 1:1s and via our feedback system.
- Document significant performance concerns within 5 business days and escalate to people-ops for coaching.
- Nominate high performers for quarterly recognition programs and compensation reviews.

Performance Improvement Plan (PIP):
- Triggered for sustained performance concerns or repeated Needs Improvement ratings.
- Typical duration: 60-90 days with weekly check-ins and documented milestones.
- People-ops reviews PIP materials and participates in off-ramps if required.

Promotion & compensation:
- Promotions require evidence of competency growth and impact; tenure is not the primary criterion.
- Compensation changes tied to promotions or market adjustments require people-ops and finance approval.

4) People policies (high-level highlights)

Probation & new-hire review:
- New hires undergo a 90-day probationary review; manager completes a formal 90-day assessment.

Remote & hybrid work:
- Redwood is remote-first; hybrid schedules are set by team leads and documented on team pages.

Time off & PTO:
- Refer to the Benefits docs for the full PTO policy. Managers should approve planned time off at least 2 weeks in advance when possible.

Security & confidentiality:
- Employees must complete security training within 7 days of start. Production access requires manager sign-off and additional training.

5) Manager guide (practical dos & don'ts)

Hiring & interviewing:
- Do: Use role scorecards and provide written rationale for decisions.
- Don't: Rely only on intuition; avoid irrelevant hypotheticals.

Onboarding & ramping:
- Do: Publish clear 30/60/90 goals and schedule weekly 1:1s.
- Do: Assign a buddy and required readings and repo walkthroughs.

Feedback & reviews:
- Do: Document feedback, reference examples, and provide next steps.
- Don't: Surprise employees during reviews; coach continuously.

Career conversations & promotions:
- Prepare evidence of sustained impact and clearly define expected scope for the next level.

Manager checklists (required):
- Pre-hire: confirm scorecard, brief interviewers, request diverse slate.
- Day 0-30: publish onboarding plan, assign buddy, schedule weekly 1:1s.
- Day 30-90: record checkpoints, complete 90-day review.
- Annual review: gather evidence, review self-assessment, prepare calibration materials.

6) Templates & example artifacts (summaries)

Included templates in people-ops library: Requisition checklist, Interview scorecard with behavioral anchors, New hire checklist, 30/60/90 plan template, Manager calibration worksheet, PIP template.

7) Governance, ownership & escalation

Ownership:
- People-ops: policy, templates, calibration facilitation, compensation governance.
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview loop, hiring decisions, onboarding execution.
- Recruiting: sourcing, offer logistics, ATS management.

Escalation paths:
- Compensation exceptions: people-ops -> finance approval for out-of-band offers.
- Performance disputes: manager -> people-ops -> HRBP -> Director escalation if unresolved.

8) Metrics & continuous improvement

Key metrics tracked monthly:
- Time-to-fill, time-to-offer, offer acceptance rate.
- New hire 90-day retention and ramp time to first PR/impact.
- Manager completion rates for 1:1s and review deadlines.

Feedback loop:
- People-ops runs quarterly manager training, gathers manager/new-hire survey data, and iterates on templates and SLAs.

Appendices (quick references):
A. Quick hiring checklist: Post req -> 3 candidate slate -> phone screen -> interviews -> panel debrief -> offer -> preboarding.
B. 30/60/90 template summary: 30: onboarding tasks + small deliverable; 60: component ownership + measurable outcome; 90: primary ownership + growth plan.
